nodes.text: Forecasters normalized with training statistics lose accuracy when the series level shifts after deployment.
Level shifts occur in deployed load forecasting [CITATION NEEDED], so the error matters in practice.
Standard pipelines normalize with training-set mean and std [CITATION NEEDED].
In the evaluations examined, normalization and capacity were changed together, so the source of shift error is not separated [search not yet run].
RQ1: Does per-window normalization reduce error under level shift without harming unshifted accuracy?
RQ2: How much of the gain depends on continuing to adapt the statistics?
Stale statistics drive the error; RWN removes most of it at no unshifted cost.
Rolling-window normalization (RWN) with capacity held fixed.
Shift sweep: s in {0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8}, 3 methods, 5 seeds, same MLP.
Ablation: RWN-fixed freezes statistics after first post-shift window (s = 0.6).
No unshifted cost.
11-29% MAE reduction for s ≤ 0.6.
No clear benefit at s = 0.8.
Two thirds of gain from re-estimating stats; one third from continued adaptation.
RQ1 answered yes for moderate shifts only.
Stale statistics rather than capacity account for much of the error (suggestive).
RQ2: continued adaptation contributes about a third.
Capacity-controlled evidence that per-window normalization removes most level-shift error up to s = 0.6, with its boundary and an attribution of the gain.
Synthetic data only.
Capacity held fixed, not varied.
Real load data; larger models.
Level shift (in training-std units); mean absolute error.

experiment_chains.hypothesis: RWN lowers error under shift with no unshifted cost
experiment_chains.falsifier: RWN no better than baseline under shift, or worse without shift
experiment_chains.design_rationale: Same model and budget for all methods isolates normalization from capacity
experiment_chains.next: If RWN helps, is it re-estimating the statistics at all, or continually adapting them? -> ablation

experiment_chains.hypothesis: Continued adaptation matters beyond a one-off re-estimate
experiment_chains.design_rationale: Freezing statistics after one window removes adaptation while keeping post-shift re-estimation
